bug_description.normalized: The saved 24-byte witness `rule r{strings:$=/.{,}?/` reaches YARA's regexp string parser with token `.{,}?`, which the regexp grammar wraps as a concat AST whose only child is a non-greedy `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` with `start = 0` and `end = 32767 (INT16_MAX)`. In vulnerable commit `459d5a2bae0f4c9a2921be0d21fe920258cb5d6d`, `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point` accepts that lone child as a chaining point because it checks only `!child->greedy`, `child->type == RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY`, and the `YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD` comparison; it does not require both siblings. The split rewires `re_ast->root_node->children_head` to `NULL` but leaves `re_ast->root_node->children_tail` pointing to `child`, also seeds the remainder AST with the same node, and then frees `child` with `yr_re_node_destroy(child)`. `yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration` immediately calls `_yr_parser_write_string` on the corrupted original AST, and `yr_re_ast_extract_literal` reloads `children_tail` and reads `child->type`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ at `libyara/re.c:369`. Commit `8eeed3ef5e2bbd5b927bf1b72879c1fa9ab979cb` fixes the bug by requiring both siblings before splitting.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed path that consumes the attacker-controlled regexp token and materializes the regex AST later handed to the chaining splitter.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact rule text `rule r{strings:$=/.{,}?/`. YARA's rule lexer reduces the `_REGEXP_` token to `str->c_string = ".{,}?"`, and line 544 passes that exact regex body into the regexp parser.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `yr_re_ast_extract_literal()` reloads `child` from the corrupted original AST's `children_tail` and dereferences the freed range node while testing whether the split result is a literal.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 4` at `libyara/re.c:369:36` in `yr_re_ast_extract_literal`.

root_cause.code: if (!child->greedy && child->type == RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY && (child->start > YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD || child->end > YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD))
root_cause.description: The split predicate accepts a large ungreedy `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` even when it is the only concat child. The vulnerable guard omits the `child->prev_sibling != NULL && child->next_sibling != NULL` precondition added by the fix, so the singleton gap node enters split logic and leaves stale AST pointers behind.
root_cause.note: For the witness regexp `.{,}?`, the concat root has exactly one child, so both sibling links are `NULL`. The fixing commit adds both sibling checks to this guard before any AST rewiring happens.

tainted_value_origin.description: AddressSanitizer allocation origin for the heap `RE_NODE` later freed in the split and reread in `yr_re_ast_extract_literal`. `re_yyparse` reaches this allocator when the witness token `.{,}?` is reduced to `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY`.

parser_admitted.description: The YARA rule parser accepts the witness far enough to reduce a regexp string declaration and invoke `yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration`; the crash happens during this reduction before the incomplete rule text would be rejected later.

fine_trace.note: This is the first project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled regexp token extracted from the rule text. For the saved witness, `str->c_string` is `.{,}?`, and this call materializes the AST later processed by the chaining splitter.

Parsing `.{,}?` takes the `single _RANGE_ '?'` reduction for `.`. `re_lexer.l` interprets `{,}` as `lo_bound = 0` and `hi_bound = INT16_MAX`, so this step allocates a `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` and stores `start = 0`, `end = 32767`, and `greedy = false`. AddressSanitizer's allocation stack points to `yr_re_node_create` reached from this reduction.

Even a one-element regexp is wrapped in `RE_NODE_CONCAT`. Appending the lone range node makes it both `children_head` and `children_tail`; because there is no second child, its `prev_sibling` and `next_sibling` remain `NULL`. This concat becomes `re_ast->root_node` when parsing returns.

fine_trace.code: if (!child->greedy && child->type == RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY && (child->start > YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD || child->end > YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD))
fine_trace.note: Root cause. The first split sees that the concat head is a non-greedy `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` with `end = 32767`, which is above `YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD` 200, and enters the split logic. The guard never checks that the candidate gap has both a left and right sibling, so it accepts the witness's singleton concat child as a chaining point.

Because the witness range node has no siblings, this rewiring makes the new remainder AST keep `children_head = child` and `children_tail = NULL`, while the original AST gets `children_head = NULL`. No statement updates the original `children_tail`, so it still aliases `child`. That original stale tail is the reference later consumed by literal extraction.

The first split frees the `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` object allocated for `.{,}?`. After this call, the original AST's `children_tail` and the remainder AST's `children_head` both dangle. AddressSanitizer's free stack points to this exact call.

fine_trace.code:
child = re_ast->root_node->children_tail;
while (child != NULL && child->type == RE_NODE_LITERAL)
fine_trace.note: Sink. `_yr_parser_write_string` calls `yr_re_ast_extract_literal(re_ast)` immediately after the split. The function reloads `child` from the corrupted original AST's `children_tail`, which still points to the freed range node from step 6, and the `child->type` read in the loop condition triggers the saved 4-byte heap-use-after-free at `libyara/re.c:369`.

poc.trigger: Feed the saved rule text to `rules_fuzzer`; during regexp string declaration reduction, YARA parses `/.{,}?/`, performs one split on the lone ungreedy range-any node, and then crashes when `_yr_parser_write_string` asks `yr_re_ast_extract_literal` to inspect the corrupted original AST.

format.name: YARA rule source text
format.contract: A textual YARA rule that reaches `yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration` with regexp token `.{,}?`, so the regexp AST is a one-child `RE_NODE_CONCAT` whose only child is an ungreedy `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` with `start = 0` and `end = INT16_MAX` (> `YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD` 200). That exact singleton split leaves `re_ast->root_node->children_tail` pointing at the freed gap node before `_yr_parser_write_string` calls `yr_re_ast_extract_literal`.
